title: Why the two-hour barrier fell
text: {{1}} was not until 2019 that a human being ran a marathon in under two hours, and the man who did it was helped by something more than training shoes {{2}} suggest. His carbon-plated racing shoes, {{3}} return energy to each stride, have since rewritten the record books, and the official world record {{4}} fallen by minutes {{5}} the technology arrived. Critics ask {{6}} the shoes amount to mechanical doping; fans reply that every era has had its edge, {{7}} the cinder track gave way to the synthetic one. What nobody disputes is the physics: a springy plate and thick foam cut the energy cost of each step, {{8}} is why the sport's governing body now sets strict limits on what a shoe may contain.
